segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “And to the angel of the assembly in Sardis write: This is what the one who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars says: I know your works: you have a name for being alive, yet you are dead.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Wake up, and strengthen what remains, which was about to die, for I have not found your works complete before my God.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Remember, then, how you received and heard; keep it, and turn back. If you do not wake up, I will come like a thief, and you will certainly not know at what hour I will come upon you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But you have a few names in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and they will walk with me in white, for they are worthy.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one who conquers will be clothed like this, in white garments, and I will never wipe their name out of the book of life, and I will acknowledge their name before my Father and before his angels.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Let anyone who has an ear hear what the Spirit is saying to the assemblies.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “And to the angel of the assembly in Philadelphia write: This is what the Holy One, the True One, says, the one who has the key of David, who opens and no one will shut, who shuts and no one opens:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know your works—look, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut—that you have little power, and yet you have kept my word and have not denied my name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Look, I am giving those from the synagogue of Satan, who say they are Jews and are not, but are lying—look, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and they will know that I have loved you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Because you have kept my word of endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole inhabited world, to test those who dwell on the earth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I am coming soon. Hold on to what you have, so that no one takes your wreath.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The one who conquers I will make a pillar in the temple of my God, and they will never go outside again; and I will write on them the name of my God and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem that comes down out of heaven from my God, and my own new name.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Let anyone who has an ear hear what the Spirit is saying to the assemblies.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “And to the angel of the assembly in Laodicea write: This is what the Amen says, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of God’s creation:

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I know your works: you are neither cold nor hot. I wish you were cold or hot!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: So, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to vomit you out of my mouth.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Because you say, ‘I am rich; I have grown rich and need nothing,’ and you do not know that you are the one who is wretched and pitiable and poor and blind and naked,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire so that you may be rich, and white garments so that you may clothe yourself and the shame of your nakedness may not be exposed, and salve to rub on your eyes so that you may see.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: All those I love, I reprove and discipline. So be zealous and turn back.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Look, I am standing at the door and knocking. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I will come in to them and dine with them, and they with me.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: To the one who conquers I will grant to sit with me on my throne, just as I also conquered and sat down with my Father on his throne.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Let anyone who has an ear hear what the Spirit is saying to the assemblies.”

notes.note: The traditional rendering is ‘church’, which is near-universal and which readers readily understand. A first-century hearer knew the word as a civic gathering and as the Septuagint’s term for Israel assembled, whereas ‘church’ now suggests a building or an institution. ‘Assembly’ is used throughout this translation so that the one Greek word is always visible.

Most modern translations render the word ‘reputation’ here, which is its sense. ‘Name’ is kept because the same word runs through the message: the ‘few names’ in Sardis (verse 4, meaning persons) and the name that will not be wiped from the book of life (verse 5). The repetition is deliberate in the Greek.

Sardis sat on a citadel thought to be impregnable, yet Greek historians record that it was captured more than once by surprise because no adequate watch was kept. Many interpreters think the call to wake up and the warning of a thief’s arrival play on that local memory, though the thief image is also a common early Christian one.

Most translations keep ‘repent’, an established term that readers understand to include a change of life. In current English the word centres on feeling sorry, while the Greek carries the prophets’ call to return to God, a change of direction in mind and conduct. ‘Turn back’ is used for that reason.

The language comes from Isaiah 22:22, where the steward Eliakim is given the key of the house of David, so that what he opens no one shuts and what he shuts no one opens. The key is the authority to admit or exclude from the royal household. Here that authority belongs to the risen Christ.

The Greek connective can mean ‘that’ or ‘because’. Taken as ‘that’, the clause states what is known about their works, with the open door as a parenthesis; taken as ‘because’, it gives the reason the door has been opened. The punctuation of the Greek edition followed here favours the first.

The phrase reflects a local conflict (compare 2:9) between this community and a synagogue in Philadelphia. The writer, himself Jewish, disputes his opponents’ right to the name; it is not a statement about Jews in general. The promise that they will bow at the assembly’s feet reverses Isaiah’s picture of the nations bowing before Israel (Isaiah 60:14; 49:23).

The Greek can mean ‘my word about endurance’, that is, Christ’s call to endure, or ‘the word of my endurance’, the message about Christ’s own steadfastness. Most modern translations take it the first way. The rendering here leaves both possible.

The traditional rendering is ‘crown’. The word normally denotes the wreath awarded to a victor in the games or worn at festivals and honours, and Revelation uses a different word, ‘diadem’, for a ruler’s crown (12:3; 19:12). ‘Wreath’ keeps the image of a prize that can be forfeited. Many scholars are content with ‘crown’, understood as a victor’s crown.

notes.traditional: the beginning of the creation of God
notes.note: The Greek word can mean ‘beginning’, ‘origin’ or ‘source’, or ‘ruler’. Translations divide among these. ‘Beginning’ is kept because it is the word’s most common sense, and Revelation later calls Christ ‘the beginning and the end’. The phrase is close to the language of Colossians 1:15–18, a letter also meant for Laodicea, where Christ is the one through whom creation came to be. It need not mean that he is the first thing created.

Many interpreters connect the image with local water: nearby Hierapolis had hot springs and Colossae had cold water, while Laodicea’s piped supply arrived tepid. On that reading both hot and cold are useful and the fault is uselessness; the older reading takes cold as hostility and lukewarm as half-heartedness. The verb that follows is the blunt ordinary word for vomiting, often softened to ‘spit’.

The three things offered answer Laodicea’s sources of pride. The city was a wealthy banking centre, was known for its wool cloth, and was associated with a medical school; an eye remedy from the region is mentioned in ancient medical writing. The link between that remedy and Laodicea itself is a reasonable inference, not a certainty.

candidates.reason: The refrain ‘the one who conquers’ closes all seven messages and recurs through Revelation and 1 John; ‘conquer’, ‘overcome’ and ‘be victorious’ are all in use and must not vary between chapters.
‘Crown’ versus ‘wreath’ affects Revelation 2:10, 4:4, Paul’s athletic imagery and the crown of thorns, and Revelation distinguishes it from διάδημα.
Translators choose between ‘worship’ and ‘bow down’ according to the object, and the choice is theologically loaded across the Gospels and Revelation.
Rendered variously as ‘patience’, ‘perseverance’, ‘steadfastness’ and ‘endurance’ across the letters and Revelation; it is a key term and should be uniform.
‘Temptation’, ‘trial’ and ‘testing’ are all traditional for this word and its verb, including in the Lord’s Prayer; one policy is needed for which sense gets which English.
